approachQuestion.prompt: A message is either an ASCII letter or an ordered list of messages. Return a fresh flat character array containing all letters in order, with list boundaries omitted. Examples: [a,[b,[],c],d] returns [a,b,c,d]; [[],[]] returns []; z returns [z].
constraints: There are n total list and letter objects including the root, 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000, and maximum list depth h ≤ 1000. The input is a finite tree without sharing.
Let L be the number of letters. List access takes constant time; copying k characters takes time proportional to k.
Do not modify the input. The output must be a fresh mutable array. Array append is amortized constant time.

options.text: Process each list's children from last to first and append letters as visited.
Create one output array. Recursively visit children in order; append a letter directly to that array when encountered, and return it after the traversal.
options.feedback: Every letter is emitted once into its final array, with no intermediate child arrays.

options.text: Return a fresh flat array from each child and concatenate child arrays into a new array at each list.
options.feedback: This preserves order and content, but repeatedly copies letters through their ancestors.

options.text: Append letters only when they are direct children of the root list.
options.feedback: [a,[b]] must include b as well as a.

feedback.reason: All calls append into the same returned buffer in child order.
details: Allocate one growable output array. A recursive visit appends a letter, or loops through a list's children in their original order and visits each. All calls share the same output array by reference. There are no returned temporary arrays or concatenations.

All calls append into the same returned buffer in child order. Returning a fresh child array and concatenating it at every ancestor could recopy a deeply nested leaf many times. Empty lists append nothing.
“Process each list's children from last to first and append letters as visited.”: [a,b] must produce [a,b], not [b,a].

“Create one output array. Recursively visit children in order; append a letter directly to that array when encountered, and return it after the traversal.”: Every letter is emitted once into its final array, with no intermediate child arrays.
“Return a fresh flat array from each child and concatenate child arrays into a new array at each list.”: This preserves order and content, but repeatedly copies letters through their ancestors.
“Append letters only when they are direct children of the root list.”: [a,[b]] must include b as well as a.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n, h, and L be as in Q1. Count active frames; exclude input and the output array including its reserved capacity. Appends have amortized constant cost, and references are passed without copying. No hashing or tail-call elimination. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: Visit all objects once and append each returned letter once.
details: Every object is visited once and each of the L letters is appended once; L ≤ n. Only the active path of call frames is auxiliary after excluding the final output buffer.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
